stories.title: The Dog Who Kept the Light
stories.fortuneLine: Old dog, old keeper, old fire on a sea of salt—the lamp does not care that the water has gone to ash.
stories.body:
The keeper died in his chair with the lamp still trimmed.

His dog waited by the door until hunger made waiting a kind of prayer, then climbed the stair as it had watched him climb, and put its paws to the wheel, and the light turned.

Ships that had expected a dark coast found a beam instead, and sailors left bread and rum at the tower door, saying the old man was still at his post.

On clear nights, those who looked up from the water saw a small shape pacing behind the glass, around and around, as if the light itself had grown a body and could not rest.

stories.title: The Last Keeper
stories.fortuneLine: Old dog, old keeper, old fire on a sea of salt—the lamp does not care that the water has gone to ash.
stories.body:
The seas burned off in a season of red dawns. Fish cooked in the shallows. The horizon went white, then was not a horizon.

The last keeper still climbed. He trimmed the wick. He wound the clockwork. He wrote in the log: “No clouds. No ships. No sea. No end.”

He wrote it every dusk, in a hand that did not change, because the duty had never named the water as a condition.

The light does not ask if the sea remains. It only asks if the stair is still there.

It was. He climbed.
